title: Epistemic Record Format, data model
description: The normative data model (SPEC.md section 3, ERF-73): what every document a corpus holds looks like once loaded, with its body attached where the model has one. Every definition refuses fields the declared version does not define, outside the x_ namespace (ERF-72). Lists total in the model may be omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-56). The reason each definition takes its shape is written on the definition. Rules over more than one record, the quote check, and the obligations on acts are in SPEC.md and cannot be stated here.

Id.description: An identifier: one or more characters, none whitespace, '"', '<', '>' or '/'. A path separator is excluded because an id names a record and never where it lives (ERF-15). Deployment-unique across record types (ERF-36).

Instant.description: An RFC 3339 instant: date, time with seconds, and offset. Seconds are mandatory because RFC 3339 makes them so and because two stances on one instant are ordered by the ledger (ERF-41).

DateOrInstant.description: A date where nothing is ordered, an instant where something is (ERF-19).

AsOfDate.description: A year, a year and month, or a full date; never more precise than the source gave (ERF-14).

HumanActor.description: A person. The id carries no '/', so it cannot also read as an agent id. A standing's `by` is this and nothing else.

AgentActor.description: A model or agent, producer/version. The producer carries no ':', so it cannot also read as a human or process id.

Actor.description: Exactly one of the three forms; they are disjoint by construction (section 2).

ActorStamp.description: Who did it, and when. The event-time key is `timestamp` everywhere; an earlier `on` was retired because a YAML 1.1 reader resolves it to the boolean true.

Verdict.description: Exactly three. A failed, unparseable or abandoned audit is never written as one: an audit that produced nothing did not happen (SPEC.md ERF-11).

CSL.description: A CSL-JSON item. Its fields are typed by CSL and preserved opaquely here (ERF-8).

auditor.description: The instrument, a bare identifier, never an Actor (ERF-11).

protocol.description: The versioned procedure; verdicts under different protocols are not comparable.

atoms_for.description: Evidence for, as the ruler faced it. Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-56).

atoms_against.description: Evidence against, as the ruler faced it. Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-56).

EvidenceAtStance.description: What the ruler faced at ruling time (ERF-20). Present and empty means stamped and faced nothing; absent means never stamped (ERF-56).

why.description: Required; an entry without a reason is a toggle. Once ERF-39; the schema is the requirement (ERF-73).

StandingEntry.description: One line of the append-only ledger (ERF-40). `timestamp` is a full instant with time and offset, never a bare date, because this is the format's only ordered ledger and a bare date and an instant on one day cannot be ordered; `by` is a person, because an LLM proposes and only a person takes a stance, and a stance speaks for one person, five endorsements being five entries; `why` is required, because an entry without a reason is a toggle and not a judgment.

tool.description: The concrete instrument, never a category (ERF-26).

hits_reported.description: The yield as the instrument reported it; text (ERF-27).

atoms.description: Atoms minted from this result. Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-56).

url.description: Where it came from, when from the web; the artifact retrieved, not a landing page. Once ERF-7; the schema is the requirement (ERF-73).

path.description: Where the corpus holds the raw file, when it does (ERF-2).

Received.description: The raw file, as it arrived (ERF-2).

Source.description: One work in the source list (ERF-2, ERF-4, ERF-6, ERF-8, ERF-68 to ERF-71).

citation_text.description: Identifies the work and never carries a URL: a citation names a work, a locator names one copy, and that is `received.url`, the artifact retrieved rather than a page describing it. A web-native work's own identity may appear as `citation.URL`. A file received by hand has no locator and no `received`.

status.description: shipped: under a permitting licence. shipped-as-quotation: as a short quotation, under no licence. not-redistributable, access-restricted, licence-unverified: an absence, with `reason` required (the conditional below). Glosses in SPEC.md section 5.

normalized.description: Path of the normalized text, relative to the source list (ERF-1, ERF-4).

reason.description: Why no normalized text is held (section 5, status vocabulary).

extraction.description: The deterministic extracting tool and exact version (ERF-70).

normalization.description: The deterministic normalizing tool and exact version (ERF-70).

then.description: A source that ships gives the path of its normalized text (ERF-4).

else.description: A source recording an absence says why (section 5, status vocabulary).

finding_audit.description: Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-55, ERF-56).

atoms_for.description: Evidence for. Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-55, ERF-56).

atoms_against.description: Evidence against. Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-55, ERF-56).

surveys.description: Surveys backing the claim (ERF-25). Total in the model; omitted on the wire when empty (ERF-55, ERF-56).

body.description: The markdown body: the proposition, then working notes. Part of the model instance; on the wire it is the file body (ERF-53).

Claim.description: One statement a person could stand behind or dispute. It has no state field: its disposition is computed from its standings (ERF-41), a claim is born with no standing and is a proposal until someone takes one, and origin that carries evidential weight is a source to cite, not a status to store.

body.description: What was sought and what was found, in prose (ERF-28). Part of the model instance; on the wire it is the file body.

Survey.description: A search act recorded as evidence of absence (section 4.5).

classification.description: An opaque label this version records and does not read (ERF-59).

CorpusDeclaration.description: Exactly one per corpus (ERF-54). `classification` is an opaque label this version records and does not read; what it means, and which corpora may cite or travel together, is deployment policy. The declaration declares no bars or gates.

sources.description: Keyed by source id, unique within the corpus (ERF-3).

SourceList.description: A corpus keeps a source list: one entry per work, keyed by a source id unique within the corpus. The top level is exactly `type` and `sources`. A source's citation, locator and normalized text live on the source and never on the atom; how the list is stored is the store's business and its interchange form the binding's.

body.description: Prose, with narrative bindings as its only structured content (ERF-31).

Narrative.description: A document, not a record: prose someone wrote, with narrative bindings as its only structured content. It has no evidence, no standings and no disposition, because nothing about it is adjudicated; a person disputes the claims it binds, not the prose. `created` takes the stamp everything else takes because who wrote it is the fact a reader most wants.

AtomId.description: An atom's id: a mint-time prefix, a hyphen, and a sequence number, e.g. kwg-117; permanent, never renamed, never reused (ERF-13).
